artboards.title: Picks · kept → also in another market

annotations.text:
BROADCAST direction — locked 3 Sep.
Graphite #0C0B10 · panels #14131A · accent #FF4D6D · live #45E0B0 · queued amber #F5C044 · chart muted #B23A52 · Archivo Expanded display, Instrument Sans body, Spline Sans Mono labels.
Static mockups: sample product is 'Loopnote' (fictional). Product: Man Friday · manfriday.app. Pricing locked at 0.7× the market leader — beta plan $34/mo after 30-day trial; remaining bracketed values ([NNN] spots, proof-band stats) await launch data. Picks (the swipe screen — renamed from 'Blitz' 4 Sep to avoid the competitor's term) is mobile-first; desktop screens share the left-rail shell. The PROTOTYPE artboard is clickable — tap through Friday's full loop: URL → brief → swipe → schedule → posted. Light editor rule: swap the hook, the voice, or a slide — never a timeline.

LANDING V2 — drafted 10 Sep, for review before any code.
What changed vs v1: (1) the URL input IS the hero call to action — a real brief in ~30s is the free tier's first step anyway; (2) a live Picks demo replaces the grey placeholder strip — reference video beside Friday's concept; (3) click attribution gets its own section (the north-star differentiator, absent from v1); (4) how-it-works tiles show the product instead of describing it; (5) the 14 languages appear in their own scripts; (6) the founding offer stands alone (book-a-call card removed 10 Sep).
Language (revised 10 Sep after review): (a) setup — Friday infers the language, shows it as a chip; the chip is a command-menu combobox (type-ahead in any script, keyboard-first), no modal, no dropdown; a 'how it sounds' control answers the Hinglish question — Hinglish / शुद्ध हिन्दी / Roman script (Sarvam Mayura code-mixed + Bulbul TTS handle all three). (b) point of use — every pick carries its language; after a keep, a bottom sheet offers 'also in' the brand's other markets, one tap = one more video (counts against the allowance). The landing band now demos this: one pick, three markets.
Home: two states of Picks-as-home — day one (no brand) and an active week (clicks first, views last; plan meter in the rail is the only plan-aware chrome). Marketing pages stay static; signed-in users land in the app, never on marketing.
Numbers (113 clicks, 41, 48.2K) are illustrative sample data.
